package_info.package_versions: all published versions (since at least Dec 4, 2023)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages abuse the npm registry by distributing large, non-software media files (movies, videos, eBooks) in violation of platform terms of service. While not containing traditional malware, they threaten the integrity and hygiene of the software supply chain by using the registry as a file hosting service for pirated or unauthorized content.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when package is downloaded or inspected)
execution_context.file_location: package root directory (multiple .ts files, e.g., video1.ts, video2.ts)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Stores and distributes large video files (likely DVD/Blu-ray rips) as part of the package contents.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Software packages are expected to contain code and necessary assets, not large media files unrelated to software functionality.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages contain JavaScript/TypeScript code and small assets, not multi-gigabyte video files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may include small demo videos or images for documentation, but not full-length movies or pirated content.
key_indicators: Presence of large .ts files in package root
Package size (~54.5 MB each) far exceeds typical code package
No corresponding code to justify media content

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when package is downloaded or inspected)
execution_context.file_location: package root directory (JSON files with timestamped Mandarin comments)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Stores time-synced user comments, likely extracted from online video streaming platforms, as part of the package contents.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Inclusion of large, unrelated user comment data is not expected in a code package and may indicate attempts to distribute pirated or unauthorized content.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not include large, unrelated user comment datasets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use might include small sample data for testing, but not full comment archives from streaming platforms.
key_indicators: Presence of large JSON files with time-synced comments
No code utilizing these comments in the package

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads npm packages with large video (.ts) files and JSON comment files, using a naming scheme (wlwz-*) to denote sequence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Packages are available for download, enabling distribution of pirated or unauthorized media via the npm registry.

attack_chain.action: Users (or automated scripts) download all related packages to reconstruct the full movie or media content.
attack_chain.leads_to: Circumvention of platform restrictions and potential copyright violations.

behavioral_signatures: Packages containing large binary media files (.ts, .mp4, etc.) unrelated to software functionality
Packages with no or minimal code but large non-code assets
Packages with naming patterns indicating sequence or partitioning (e.g., wlwz-*)
file_indicators: Large (>50MB) JSON files with time-synced comments
Packages with total size >50MB and minimal code
network_indicators: No direct network indicators (distribution occurs via npm registry itself)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Flag packages that contain large binary media files (e.g., .ts, .mp4) or large JSON data unrelated to code, especially when package size exceeds typical thresholds (e.g., >10MB). Look for packages with minimal or no code and naming patterns suggesting partitioned media distribution. Automated scanning of package contents for non-code assets and size anomalies can help detect this abuse.
